correctness.rationale: Positivity of the radius and first-harmonic closure give a convex closed boundary, and the mean constraint fixes the length. On the shorter angular arc the perturbation chord is bounded by a constant times ||f||∞ times the unperturbed chord length, giving integrable derivatives and a continuous second variation. The chord double integral has normalization (2π)^−3, hence circular value 2/π². An independent calculation used arclength x=θ+ε sin(mθ)/m for f=cos(mθ). The inverse angle is x−ε sin(mx)/m+ε² sin(mx)cos(mx)/m+O(ε³). At arclength gap u, the mean second-order tangential contribution to the chord length is −sin(u/2)/(2m²), and the mean transverse-norm correction is (A+B)^2/[8m² sin(u/2)], with A,B as in the record. This gives Q_m=(2−J_+)/m², where J_+=1/4[I_{m+1}/(m+1)^2+I_{m−1}/(m−1)^2+2(I_m−2)/(m²−1)] and I_k=2Σ_{j≤k}1/(2j−1), by product-to-sum and telescoping. Exact algebra gives the same closed Q_m, including 44/135 and 4/21. The square bound gives J_+≤1/(m+1)+1/(m−1)≤4/3, so Q_m>0 for all m≥2; I_k=O(log k) gives the claimed error term. Rotations diagonalize the quadratic form with equal sine and cosine weights, and uniform Fourier approximation and continuity pass the result to the fixed C² inputs.
residual_risks: Strict negativity is for nonzero admissible directions. The little-o is for each fixed perturbation; no frequency-uniform or global stability claim.

value.rationale: The second variation quantifies a known geometric extremum in the intrinsic curvature radius, separating directional strictness from the absence of an L² spectral gap. The exact coefficient for every harmonic and its inverse-square law are the information needed to compare near-circle deficits or to choose an appropriate local stability norm; a qualitative global maximum gives neither.
